item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 14, 2026
item.description:
With the latest from across the media business, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
The Country Music Association has announced its 2026 Broadcast Awards winners, with Country star Zach Top personally calling the honorees. For National Personality of the Year, Buzz Brainard's Highway Hot 30 Countdown won the weekly category, while Big D and Bubba took daily honors. In local personality awards, The Andie Summers Show on WXTU Philadelphia won Major Market. The Jesse and Anna Show on WUBE Cincinnati took Large Market. Steve and Gina on KXKT Omaha won Medium Market, and Officer Don and DeAnn on WBUL Lexington earned Small Market honors. Station of the Year winners include KSCS Dallas for Major Market, WQDR Raleigh for Large Market, KXKT Omaha for Medium Market, and WKML Fayetteville for Small Market. All winners will be recognized November 18th during the 60th Annual CMA Awards in Nashville.
Meanwhile,
Northwestern University's latest Medill report finds local news deserts are growing at their fastest pace in five years. Twenty-six additional U.S. counties lost their last locally based news source, bringing the total to 238. Newspaper closures now average three per week, while employment continues to decline. Researchers also found that ten broadcasting groups control three-quarters of local TV newsrooms.
In television news,
TEGNA and Disney Entertainment Television have renewed ABC affiliation agreements for 13 TEGNA stations in a multi-year deal. The stations include WFAA in Dallas, KVUE in Austin and WZZM in Grand Rapids. TEGNA says the agreement extends its long-standing partnership with Disney
Turning to radio,
Cumulus Media has promoted Kathy “KB” Brown to Vice President of Urban Formats. Brown will oversee programming for 40 stations nationwide across Urban Mainstream, Urban AC, Classic Hip Hop and Gospel formats. She'll also continue as Program Director and On-Air Talent for Z93 JAMZ and Magic 107.3 in Charleston, South Carolina. Brown joined Cumulus in 2017 and brings extensive major-market programming experience to the position.
Turning to industry honors,
The 2026 International Women’s Podcast Awards honored outstanding audio storytelling during a ceremony in Toronto. Freedom Needs a Soundtrack earned two awards for visionary leadership and insight from a role model. Other winners included Debt Heads for comedy, Everybody Knows But Me for storytelling, Points North for behind-the-scenes brilliance, and Two-Faced: John of God for pure emotion. Well Beyond Medicine received the award for Changing the World One Moment at a Time.
Recognizing achievement across the media industry,
The New York Times has won two Gerald Loeb Awards for excellence in business and financial journalism. The newspaper earned top honors for investigative reporting examining financial benefits tied to President Trump and for breaking news coverage of his Liberation Day tariffs. Times journalists were also finalists in seven additional categories, including international reporting, personal finance and visual storytelling. The awards recognize outstanding business and economic journalism.
In awards and recognition news,
The Radio Hall of Fame has welcomed eight new members. The Class of 2026 includes Boomer Esiason, Dennis Green, Shotgun Tom Kelly, Helen Little, Bob Pittman, Rickey Smiley, Charlie Van Dyke and Fred Winston. Bobby Bones hosted the induction ceremony October eighth in Chicago, celebrating the broadcasters and executives who helped shape radio.
And finally,
The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has named Tatti Ribeiro and Noora Niasari recipients of its 2026 Gold Fellowship for Women, presented with CHANEL. Ribeiro earned recognition for her debut film, Valentina, while Niasari directed the award-winning Shayda. The yearlong fellowship provides mentorship, networking and career development opportunities for emerging women filmmakers.
For more industry news, the latest media jobs and free tools, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
